subject: Greenwave: clarifying Order Form/MAA redlines on output rights & training consent
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenwavehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@greenwavehealth.com>, legal@greenwavehealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redlines to MSA/Order Form - output/training questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Our legal team attached a marked-up MSA and the order form with a couple of specific asks around IP and model training. High-level summary:
- We need clarity that Greenwave retains ownership of customer-provided data and of model outputs generated from our inputs.
- We want an explicit opt-out for Redwood using any customer data or outputs to further train your models (no training without affirmative consent).
- We're asking for a limited feedback license for Redwood to use anonymized telemetry for quality/bug fixes, but not for model training.

Attached: Greenwave_Redline_MSA_v2.docx; OrderForm_Greenwave_20270409.pdf; redlines_summary.xlsx

Can you confirm Redwood's stance on each point and, if acceptable, propose precise language we can include in the order form or an addendum? If not acceptable, please flag the sections where you'd prefer alternate language.

We'd like to turn this quickly — our procurement deadline is COB next Friday (2027-04-16).

Thanks,
Alex

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Rishi (Sales lead), Priyom (Legal), and Laura (Product/compliance) to help with the details.

Quick note on timeline: we're aiming to produce proposed language and a brief internal risk call by Monday EOD (2027-04-12) so you have something concrete early next week.

Internal asks for the group (copied):
- Confirm whether we can accept customer ownership of outputs in the Order Form vs MSA carveout.
- Draft opt-out language for training use and propose an operational opt-out process (e.g., config flag, contract opt-out, or separate data-handling SOW).
- Provide a short explanation of what we would consider "anonymized telemetry" and whether that could be used for model improvements vs. only for product analytics/bug fixes.

Alex — we'll send proposed wording once internal alignment is complete.

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA/Order Form - output/training questions

Kimberly / team —

I reviewed Greenwave's marked MSA and their summary. High-level thoughts:
1) Output ownership: We can accept a contract stating that customer owns "Outputs" defined as responses generated from Customer Input, provided we keep a narrow reservation that Redwood may retain copies for debugging, fraud detection, and compliance for the contract term (not for model training) unless explicit training consent is given. Proposed clause: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Redwood's use of Outputs is limited to providing the Service, debugging, security, and compliance; any use of Outputs for model training or model improvement requires Customer's prior written consent."

2) Training/data use opt-out: Acceptable as an affirmative opt-in model. Operationally we should: (a) allow an Order Form checkbox or addendum that opts in to "Training & Model Improvement"; (b) by default, Customer data and Outputs are excluded from model training. That aligns with enterprise expectations and avoids surprising customers.

3) Feedback/telemetry license: We should offer Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated/anonymized telemetry for product improvement and safety testing, but exclude that from model training unless the customer opts in. Define "aggregated/anonymized telemetry" as: metrics, usage patterns, and de-identified error logs that cannot be traced to a person or Customer dataset.

4) Practical fallback: If Customer refuses training use entirely, we can still accept the deal with a modest fee uplift (suggest +10–15% on per-token pricing) to offset model-improvement overhead. Recommend Rishi owns commercial discussion.

I'll draft precise language in a short doc and attach to Kimberly's reply.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenwavehealth.com>, legal@greenwavehealth.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:10:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed wording and next steps (Greenwave Order Form)

Alex / Greenwave legal —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a short set of proposed clauses (Redwood_proposed_clauses.docx) aligned with Priyom's notes. Key points included:
- Customer Ownership of Outputs: clear sentence retaining ownership; Redwood limited to operational uses; explicit prohibition on training without written opt-in.
- Training Opt-in Mechanism: Order Form checkbox + signature on an addendum. Default = Opt-out.
- Telemetry/Feedback License: narrow, non-exclusive license for aggregated/anonymized telemetry for product quality and bug fixes; expressly excluded from model training.
- Commercial fallback: if Customer prohibits all training-related uses, Redwood reserves the right to propose an adjusted pricing schedule to account for lost model-improvement benefits.

If this looks close to acceptable, can you confirm which route you'd like — (A) accept clauses as written and sign the Order Form with the training opt-out default, or (B) request redline edits to the proposed text?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm preference by Wed 2027-04-14 COB.
- If edits requested, we'll circulate final redline by Thu and route to DocuSign.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_clauses.docx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Deals — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenwavehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@greenwavehealth.com, Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@greenwavehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed wording and next steps (Greenwave Order Form)

Kimberly —

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic approach. Two quick clarifications from our side:
1) The telemetry definition looks OK, but can you confirm that de-identified logs will be retained only for operational troubleshooting and not used to surface product improvements in the model training pipeline?
2) On the pricing uplift: can you outline the likely commercial impact range and whether that would be a fixed uplift or a % change to per-token rates?

If you can provide short answers to those two items we'll share with procurement and legal and aim to confirm by Thu.

— Alex

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenwavehealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed wording and next steps (Greenwave Order Form)

Alex / team —

Short answers to Alex's points:
1) Telemetry retention/use: Correct — de-identified and aggregated telemetry will be retained for operational/troubleshooting and product analytics only. We will not feed de-identified telemetry into the model training pipeline unless Greenwave expressly opts in via the Order Form addendum. We'll add a one-line guarantee to the Clause: "De-identified or aggregated telemetry will not be used for model training or model improvement absent Customer's explicit opt-in."

2) Pricing uplift: Commercially, we'd expect a 10–15% uplift on list per-token pricing if no model-training access is granted. Execution: percentage increase applied to per-token rates for the term, rather than a fixed one-time fee. Rishi will lead the commercial proposal and can provide a price schedule.

If that works, Kimberly — please share the updated clause with the one-line guarantee and the commercial uplift language so Alex's team can review before Thu.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Policy — Redwood Inference
